label: disabled-code-left-in
name: Commented-out statements or #if 0 blocks added or kept in the diff
description: What breaks: dead text a reader must parse and that may hide a disabled check. `// k_xfers_completed = 0;` duplicated in header and source (2737826254); `// wait_for_hbm_vwrite_complete(...)` kept as a possible alternative (2737935271 'Or are you leaving as reference for an alternative strategy?'); the `if (pdc + 1 == dev->num_fetchers)` guard commented out instead of deleted (2771711406); an #if 0 block of spdlog::debug in a constructor loop (2915191812 'can we get rid of this dead code?'); new debug logging under #if 0 (3102601258 'if this isn't useful, should get rid of it'); a pre-existing warn/check block wrapped in #if 0, which also removes a check the body does not mention (3102603313); #if 0 plus commented dump calls after REQUIRE lines in a test (2620242347 'can this go away?'). Procedure: flag added lines that are `//` plus code syntax (an identifier followed by `(` or `=` and `;`, `// if`, `// }`), added `#if 0`, and removed code lines that reappear as comments in the same hunk; ask delete-or-explain; when the disabled code was a check or a wait, report the behavior change separately (see silent-behavior-change).
disposition_reason: Check 10 asks whether a hunk belongs to the feature; disabled code belongs to no feature and is found by a regex, a different procedure. 7 rows over 5 PRs.
agent_feasibility: yes: regex over added lines; fully mechanical.

members.concern: Commented-out assignments `k_xfers_completed = 0; v_xfers_completed = 0;` are added to PosDevice::init while the matching members are also declared (commented) in device.hpp; Wade asks why both places carry them and whether they are needed at all.

detection.trigger: Added lines that are commented-out code (`// name = value;`, `// call(...)`) rather than prose comments, in a production source or header.
detection.procedure: grep the diff's added lines for `^\+\s*//\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*\s*(=|\()` ; for each hit grep the identifier across h/ and src/ to see whether a live or commented declaration exists elsewhere; if no live use exists, ask for removal.
detection.question: Is this commented-out code used or declared live anywhere, or is it residue of a debug effort that the PR no longer needs?

members.quote: do we need these in both the header and the impl file? This cpp file already includes `device.hpp` where they're also declared
members.note: src/pos/device.cpp is not in the final file list (8 files), so the author removed the hunk before the approved head. Wade read device.hpp (not in the diff hunk shown) to know the members are declared there.

detection.trigger: Added lines that are commented-out code (a call or assignment behind `//`) in a production header, especially an old form of a function the PR also changed.
detection.procedure: grep the diff's added lines for `^\+\s*//\s*[a-z_]+\(` ; for each, check whether a live call with the same name exists nearby (then the comment is a stale alternative); ask whether it is intentional reference or residue.
detection.question: Is this commented-out call residue, or a deliberately kept alternative that a comment should say so?

members.quote: can probably remove the above comments? Or are you leaving as reference for an alternative strategy?
members.note: At the approved head the commented call is still present at hwattention.hpp:655 and a commented wait_for_hbm_vwrite_complete signature at :443. He offers the author both readings (remove, or state it is deliberate) rather than ordering removal.

detection.trigger: An added line in the diff is a comment whose text is syntactically code (starts with `// if`, `// }`, `// <identifier>(`), or a removed code line reappears as an added `//`-prefixed line in the same hunk.
detection.procedure: For each hunk, compare removed lines with added lines after stripping a leading `//`; also grep the added lines for `^\s*//\s*(if|for|while|}|[A-Za-z_]+\()`. Confirm the commented text is not a prose comment by checking it parses as C++.
detection.question: Is this added comment line a piece of code that the PR disabled rather than an explanation, and does nothing in the PR body say it is kept on purpose?

At the approved head c502e4d61a both are gone and replaced by a prose comment: 'wait after every transfer for now. This is needed to work around a chip hang and should be reduced once we have an updated bitfile.' Matches PR body line 'Add workaround to avoid HBM hang issue on v-cache transfers'.

members.concern: An #if 0 block of spdlog::debug statements (compiled-out debug code) sits inside the hwkv_rings constructor loop; Wade asks to remove the dead code.

detection.trigger: The diff adds or keeps, inside a changed region, a block under #if 0, a commented-out statement block, or an #ifdef on a macro nothing defines.
detection.procedure: grep the diff's added lines for '#if 0', '// spdlog', '//   ' prefixed statements; for an #ifdef macro, grep h/ src/ CMakeLists.txt for its definition. If nothing defines it and no comment says why it is kept, ask for removal.
detection.question: Does any build configuration ever compile this block, and if not, why does it stay in the file?

members.note: At commit 4491ff73db h/pos/hwattention.hpp:507-516 is an '#if 0 ... #endif' block of four spdlog::debug calls inside the k_ring/v_ring init loop. The digest shows no hunk for this comment, so whether the PR added the block or only touched nearby lines is not established from the digest. Author reply: 'the ifdeffed out debug block. sure.'

members.concern: A block of debug logging (spdlog::debug of pass/device/rel_tok_ix at layer 0) is added inside `#if 0 ... #endif`; Wade says dead code that is not useful should be deleted rather than kept disabled.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a line `#if 0` (or wraps existing lines in `#if 0 ... #endif`), i.e. compiled-out code with a literal-false condition rather than a named macro or runtime flag.
detection.procedure: grep the diff for '^\+#if 0'. For each hit read the enclosed block to its #endif: classify as debug logging, a disabled check, or disabled production logic. Check that no named build option or env var can enable it (literal 0 cannot). Check whether the block is new in the PR or wraps code that existed at BASE (git show BASE:FILE). Flag each block; the ask is delete it, or gate it behind a named macro / log level / env var so it can be turned on without editing source.
detection.question: Can this disabled block be enabled by anything other than editing the source, and if not, why is it in the tree instead of deleted (or behind a named switch)?

members.quote: if this isn't useful, should get rid of it

members.concern: Same ask as 3102601258: a pre-existing warn/check block in prepare_hwattn_cmds (the worker-side function that builds hardware attention commands) is now wrapped in `#if 0`; delete it if it is not useful.

detection.trigger: The diff adds `#if 0` around lines that exist at BASE (disabling code by preprocessor instead of deleting it).
detection.procedure: Same as 3102601258; additionally diff the enclosed lines against BASE to confirm they are pre-existing code being switched off rather than new debug code. For a disabled check (here: a warn when tok_ix < MIN_TOK_IDX_FOR_HWATTN), note that the condition it guarded is now silently unchecked.
detection.question: Is this disabled block dead code to delete, and does disabling it remove a check the PR body does not say it removes?

members.note: Code fact at 9d0d649274 worker.cpp:769-777: `#if 0` wraps `if (workreq->tok_ix < hardware::MIN_TOK_IDX_FOR_HWATTN) { spdlog::warn(...); //tron::hardware::debug_exit(...) }`; the warn existed at BASE (the diff shows only `+#if 0` added above it), so this hunk disables an existing warning rather than adding debug code. No direct reply on this thread; the author's reply on 3102601258 ('I just wrapped it in an if to turn it on and off') covers both, so author_outcome is taken from that thread. Wade did not raise the second half (a lost warning); he only repeated the dead-code ask.

members.concern: Right after the REQUIRE lines the new test carries an '#if 0' block (compiled-out code) plus commented-out debug dump calls; he asks whether the disabled code can be deleted.

detection.trigger: Added lines contain '#if 0', '#if false', a block of commented-out statements (lines starting with '// ' followed by code such as 'std::string', 'debug_', a function call with ';'), or a '/* ... */' block holding code or pasted log output.
detection.procedure: grep the added lines for '^\+#if 0', '^\+\s*// .*;\s*$' (commented-out statements), and '^\+\s*/\*' blocks longer than 3 lines whose content looks like code or log lines. For each block, check whether a comment above it says why it is kept (a documented manual-debug switch). If not, ask for removal.
detection.question: Is there a stated reason this disabled code must stay in the tree, or is it leftover from development?
